usage.callShape: POST https://agents.allium.so/api/v1/explorer/queries/run-async with JSON body {"parameters":{"sql":"<SQL query string>"}} -> returns {run_id}. Then GET /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/status (FREE) until "succeeded", then GET /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/results (SEPARATE x402 paid ~$0.01) for the rows.
usage.outputShape: Submit: body.run_id (string). Status poll: body is a bare JSON string ("queued"|"running"|"succeeded"|...). Results: body.data[] (rows), body.sql (echoed query).
quirks: Async multi-step flow: the run-async endpoint only submits and returns {run_id} — it does NOT return rows.
Body shape is {"parameters":{"sql":"..."}} — the SQL goes inside parameters.sql, not at top level.
Status endpoint GET /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/status is FREE and returns a bare JSON string like "queued" then "running" then "succeeded". Poll it (no payment) until succeeded.
Fetching results requires a SECOND paid x402 call: GET /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/results (~$0.01 USDC). So a full query costs ~$0.02 total across two paid calls.
Note path differs: submit uses /queries/run-async but status+results use /query-runs/{run_id}/... (GET /queries/{run_id}/results returns 404).
Observed price was $0.01 per call (registry listed 0.03/Varies).
Accepts USDC on Base (eip155:8453), Solana, and X Layer (eip155:196).
usage.guide: Submit a raw SQL query by POSTing JSON {"parameters":{"sql":"SELECT ... LIMIT n"}} to https://agents.allium.so/api/v1/explorer/queries/run-async (x402 paid, ~$0.01). Read run_id from the response. Then poll GET /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/status (free) until it returns "succeeded". Finally GET /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/results (a SECOND x402 paid call, ~$0.01) and read the rows from body.data[]. Use small queries with LIMIT — this runs against indexed blockchain data tables (e.g. ethereum.blocks, crosschain.metrics.overview).
